title: Awake: Hello Windows Facial Recognition Not Working After Screen Turns Off
author: github-monkey
summary: The Awake + Windows Hello failure is specific enough for a maintainer-side reproduce pass: only Awake is enabled, the affected mode is indefinite keep-awake, Windows Hello is enabled, and the public thread already includes a bug-report ZIP.

judgment.rationale: The current public report already gives a concrete single-module setup and a consistent failure after the display turns off, so the next step is maintainer-side repro and power-transition tracing rather than another generic reporter request.
evidence: The issue says only Awake is enabled, the machine is on Windows 11 25H2, and Awake is set to keep the system awake indefinitely.
Windows Hello facial recognition stops working only after the screen turns off and recovers only after a restart or a full sleep/power-cycle reset.
The issue includes a PowerToys bug-report ZIP and no discussion suggesting the ask is waiting on the reporter.
Current Awake code uses SetThreadExecutionState with ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED and optionally ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED, plus a reapply path after power events.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the Hello/display-off flow on a Hello-enabled machine and inspect Awake's power-request transition handling before asking the reporter for anything else.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys fix is plausible because Awake is directly responsible for the power-request state during the failing display-off path, but the exact transition that strands Windows Hello still needs maintainer-side debugging.

issue_context.summary: With only Awake enabled, Windows Hello facial recognition stops working after the display turns off and does not recover until the device is restarted or fully cycled through sleep/power state reset.
known_information: The issue identifies the module as Awake and supplies Windows 11 25H2 build information.
The reporter explicitly says only Awake is enabled and that the mode is keep awake indefinitely.
A public PowerToys bug-report ZIP is attached.
No assignee, labels beyond Product-Awake, or linked fix attempt are present.
inferences: Because keyboard and touchpad still work, the machine is not in a full unrecoverable sleep state when the Hello failure occurs.
The failure is likely tied to display-off and resume behavior while Awake keeps the system out of sleep, not to a generic inability to use Windows Hello at all.
issue_context.analysis: This is best treated as reproducible. The remaining uncertainty is internal power-transition behavior that maintainers can investigate locally using the existing public report and bug-report ZIP.
initial_investigation: src/modules/Awake/Awake/Core/Manager.cs computes Awake state with ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED and optionally ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED, which is the exact layer that can change how the system behaves when the display turns off.
The same file also has a ReapplyAwakeState() path for power events, so lock/display-off transitions are already recognized as meaningful state boundaries inside Awake.
Nothing in the public thread suggests a missing repro description; the unknown is the internal wake/display transition, not what the reporter did.

actions.label: Approve Awake / Windows Hello investigation
actions.note: The report is solid, but the hypothesis remains low-confidence until a maintainer traces the display-off transition locally.

actions.label: Reproduce Windows Hello failure after Awake display-off
actions.note: Use a Hello-enabled Windows 11 machine with only Awake enabled and let the display turn off while Awake is active.

prerequisites: Use a Windows 11 machine with Windows Hello face unlock enabled.
Set Awake to keep the system awake indefinitely while allowing the display to turn off.
steps: Wait until the display turns off naturally.
Attempt to unlock the machine with Windows Hello facial recognition.
If Hello fails, verify that keyboard and touchpad still respond and then compare with the same flow after disabling Awake.
reproduce.expected_result: Windows Hello should continue to unlock the device normally after display-off while Awake is enabled; PowerToys should not require a restart or full sleep cycle to recover face recognition.

proposed_fixes.title: Verify Awake's keep-awake power request does not strand Windows Hello after display-off
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The current best hypothesis is that Awake's continuous system-required state through display-off and unlock transitions is interacting badly with the Windows Hello resume path, leaving face recognition unavailable until the power state is fully reset.
plan: Reproduce the issue on a Windows Hello-enabled machine with Awake in indefinite mode and the display allowed to turn off.
Trace Awake's lock/unlock and power-event handling to confirm whether execution-state reapply or cleanup leaves Hello in the bad state.
If confirmed, add the narrowest transition-aware reset or reapply behavior needed so Hello resumes normally after display-off while Awake is active.
verification: Enable Awake in the affected mode, let the screen turn off, and confirm Windows Hello still unlocks the device normally afterward.
Disable Awake and re-run the same scenario to verify the fix is scoped to the problematic Awake transition rather than hiding an unrelated Hello issue.

confidence.rationale: The issue is concrete and reproducible, but the public evidence does not yet identify which specific power/display transition causes Windows Hello to stop recovering.
